{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Outsourcing Agreement (M&I)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of the M&I Outsourcing Agreement — verified findings

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have completed a playbook review of the Outsourcing Agreement. Of the 18 rules assessed, **13 are deviations** requiring redlines and **5 are compliant** (non-compete, audit, MFN, auto-renewal, and — favourably — the absence of any Customer MFN obligation).

The agreement is structurally vendor-favourable in four respects that drive most of the risk:

- **Liability is one-sided and thin.** The only cap (§ 13.4) limits M&I alone, is set at three months' payments (below our six-month floor), and has no carve-outs for indemnity, confidentiality, gross negligence or willful misconduct. That cap also applies "notwithstanding any provision in this Agreement", which functionally guts M&I's otherwise strong § 14.2(B) indemnity.
- **We are locked in for eight years with no realistic exit.** § 10.3(A) requires us to source all Monthly Base Fee Services from M&I for the full Term with no descope right; § 8.1(ii)/§ 8.13 impose a minimum monthly fee payable in advance; and the only exit (§ 11.1) demands one year's notice plus a percentage of Estimated Remaining Value, expressly outside the cap. Two Customer-payable termination fees are deemed liquidated damages under § 13.5.
- **We do not own or control what we pay for, and we cannot get our data back.** § 10.4 vests in M&I every work of authorship created in performing the Services even where we funded it, and permits resale to other M&I customers; § 17.2 confines us to Term-only use. Separately, no provision anywhere requires M&I to return or export Customer Data on exit. (Customer Data *ownership* is protected under § 17.1, and § 17.4 restricts M&I's use of our Confidential Information.)
- **Ancillary terms need alignment.** M&I's home forum (Wisconsin), asymmetric assignment rights, an over-broad all-employee non-solicit, no stated warranty period or warranty remedy, no source-code licence coverage for Affiliates or successors, and no E&O or cyber cover.

Five deviations sit in or near **walk-away territory** and are listed in section 3. Note that three section references and several quantum figures are **redacted** in the source; we have flagged these and reserve comment (including on § 11.3, "Following Change in Control of Customer", which is redacted and unreviewable).

---

## 2. Findings table

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary of position |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | *Redacted* (relates to §§ 10.4, 17.1–17.2, 17.4) | § 10.4 vests custom development in M&I even where we pay, and permits resale to other M&I customers; § 17.2 limits us to Term-only use. Add a numbered § 10.5 perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense Developed Software, with a conforming carve-out in § 17.2. |
| 2 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Cap, mutuality and carve-outs | Deviation | § 13 DAMAGES | § 13.4 caps M&I alone at three months' payments (below the six-month floor), with no carve-outs beyond collection of amounts due. Make the cap mutual, move to 12 months' payments, and place indemnity, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct outside the cap. The § 13.2 mutual consequential-damages waiver is already in place. |
| 3 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 10 MODIFICATION OR TERMINATION OF SERVICES | § 10.3(A) requires us to source all Monthly Base Fee Services from M&I for the eight-year Term, with no descope right and no performance-based exit — while §§ 3.1–3.2 let M&I perform through Affiliates and third parties. Replace with express freedom to source from M&I or any other provider. |
| 4 | High | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 14 INSURANCE AND INDEMNITY | Scope and defence procedures (§§ 14.2(B), 14.3) are strong, but the § 13.4 three-month cap applies and there is no procure/modify/replace or refund remedy. Add infringement continuity remedies and carve the indemnity out of the cap with a 3x annual fees super-cap. |
| 5 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Deviation | § 13 DAMAGES | § 13.5 deems both the § 11.1 Convenience Fee and the § 11.2(A) Cause Fee liquidated damages, each a *redacted* percentage of Estimated Remaining Value and each outside the cap. Cap the single fee at three months' average Fees, align the § 11.1 scoping sentence, substitute it for the Cause Fee, and state exclusivity once in § 13.5. |
| 6 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 23 SOURCE CODE | The § 23.4 escrow licence is non-transferable (reinforced by § 23.5(1)) and runs to "Customer" alone. Extend to Affiliates on written notice and make it transferable to an M&A successor, conforming § 23.5(1). |
| 7 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 11 TERMINATION | § 11.1 requires one year's notice plus a percentage of Estimated Remaining Value, unamortized Conversion costs and disposition Expenses, outside the cap; § 10.2 lets M&I withdraw non-Core Services mid-term on 90 days' notice. Cut our notice to 90 days, cap the fee at three months' average Fees, delete the add-on costs, and limit M&I's withdrawal right to the end of the Term. |
| 8 | High | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Deviation | *Redacted* (relates to §§ 11.4, 17.1, 17.5) | § 11.4 transition assistance meets the preferred position on trigger, duration and rates, but **no provision requires return or export of Customer Data on exit**. Insert a § 11.5 requiring return within 30 days in machine-readable format plus certified deletion. |
| 9 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | **Compliant** | § 21.4 | No non-compete or field-of-use covenant binds us; §§ 21.7(B) and 23.5 are conventional scope-of-use limits. Sits at the preferred position; no redline. |
| 10 | Medium | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 22 MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS | § 22.4 lets M&I freely assign on merger, reorganization or asset sale, while our carve-out requires a $100,000,000-capital financial institution affiliate and § 21.11 compliance. Make successor assignment mutual on written notice, keeping consent (not unreasonably withheld) for all other assignments. |
| 11 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 22 MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS | §§ 22.1–22.2 select Wisconsin law and exclusive venue in Milwaukee County / E.D. Wis. — M&I's home forum, outside the accepted list. Move to New York law and exclusive venue in New York County. No arbitration agreement exists (Article 15 is non-binding escalation). |
| 12 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Deviation | § 10 MODIFICATION OR TERMINATION OF SERVICES | § 8.1(ii) minimum monthly fee + § 10.3(A) eight-year sourcing duty with no reduction right = multi-year take-or-pay. Confine the commitment to the current 12-month period, add a 30-day reduction right, and true up shortfalls instead of penalising them. |
| 13 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Deviation | § 22 MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS | § 22.14 is mutual and solicitation-only (good), but covers **all** employees for the whole Term with no advertising carve-out. Narrow to personnel directly involved in the Services for 12 months after involvement ends, and add general-advertisement and unsolicited-approach carve-outs. |
| 14 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 16.1 (By M&I) | Express warranties exist and the § 16.1(F) disclaimer is carved back, but no warranty period is stated and there is no warranty remedy (§ 12.3 offers only escalation or termination plus capped Damages). Insert § 16.1(G): 90 days for reports, 30 days for Services, with repair/replace or, at our election, refund. |
| 15 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | **Compliant** | § 21.4 | M&I has no audit right over us; § 21.8(B)–(C) and § 17.1 run in our favour. At or better than preferred; no redline. Noted commercially: § 21.8 regulatory-examination cost reimbursement and § 21.7(C)(ii) books-and-records evidence. |
| 16 | Medium | MFN — MFN obligations burdening Customer | **Compliant** | § 8 FEES | No MFN or most-favoured-pricing mechanic in either direction. Preferred position; an MFN in our favour would be an optional ask only. |
| 17 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | **Compliant** | § 2 TERM | No auto-renewal; § 2.2 renewal requires mutual written agreement, and the only unilateral extension option is ours (12 months at then-current terms on five months' notice). Preferred position. For the file: the eight-year initial term is long and the notice choreography is front-loaded. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Deviation | § 14 INSURANCE AND INDEMNITY | § 14.1(A) is otherwise robust (CGL $2m, fidelity $10m, WC/EL $500k, all-risk property, A-rated carriers, 30 days' notice), but there is **no E&O and no cyber/privacy cover** for a vendor processing our customer data. Add E&O $1m and cyber/privacy $2m to the § 14.1(A) list; § 14.1(B) certificates pick them up automatically. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following deviations reach walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as non-negotiable minima rather than trading chips:

1. **Exclusivity for the full eight-year Term with no performance-based exit** (§ 10.3(A)) — exclusive dealing for the whole term, aggravated by M&I's freedom to subcontract under §§ 3.1–3.2.
2. **Multi-year take-or-pay with no reduction right** (§ 8.1(ii), § 8.13, § 10.3(A)) — the only escape is the § 11.1 penalty, not a true-up.
3. **No Customer Data return on exit** — no provision anywhere in the Agreement requires return or export; § 17.1 confirms ownership only and § 17.5 addresses security only.
4. **Liability cap below the six-month floor, one-sided, with no carve-outs** (§ 13.4) — also at or near walk-away as it applies "notwithstanding any provision in this Agreement" and neutralises the § 14.2(B) indemnity.
5. **Customer-payable liquidated damages on both convenience and cause terminations, expressly outside the cap** (§ 13.5 with §§ 11.1, 11.2(A)) — at or near walk-away; one fee is triggered by our own Event of Default.
6. **All-employee non-solicit** (§ 22.14) — the scope element alone is walk-away; scope and duration must both come down.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline.** Thirteen deviations carry drafted proposals; four were repaired during verification (IP, LD, T4C, WARRANTY) and should be re-read in context before release, particularly the § 10.5 insertion and the § 11.1/§ 11.2(A)/§ 13.5 cross-reference chain.
2. **Sequence the negotiation around the six walk-away items.** We recommend presenting exclusivity/minimum commitment, the liability cap and carve-outs, the termination-fee quantum, and data return as a single linked package, since the § 13.4 cap and the § 11.1 fee mechanic interact.
3. **Obtain the redacted provisions before we sign off.** We need unredacted text for § 11.3 ("Following Change in Control of Customer"), the § 11.1/§ 11.2(A) fee percentages, the § 9.2(D) Service Level Credits, and the sections shown as redacted for the IP and Transition findings. We reserve comment on any fee or right they carry.
4. **Confirm insurability with M&I's broker** for the added E&O and cyber/privacy lines before finalising § 14.1(A) amounts.
5. **Calendar the Term mechanics** now: the § 2.2 choreography (M&I proposal 18 months out, our response within six months, option exercise five months out) and the § 11.4 six-month transition trigger require diligent diarising on our side even if the term length is not reduced.
6. **Flag for the business, not for redline:** the § 21.8 regulatory-examination cost reimbursement, § 21.7(C)(ii) books-and-records evidence, § 21.11(A) new-Affiliate Conversion Expenses and Fees, § 21.11(B) post-change-of-control scope cap, and the at-our-expense basis and 100-day election notice in § 11.4.

Favourable terms we are deliberately preserving and should not trade away: the mutual § 13.2 consequential-damages waiver; the absence of any Vendor audit, MFN or non-compete right over us; our § 17.1 Customer Data ownership and § 17.4 confidentiality protections; the Customer-only renewal option in § 2.2; the unqualified § 14.2(B) indemnity (no Customer-modification, combination or specification exclusions); no fee on an M&I Event of Default (§ 11.2(B)); and the penalty-free Disaster exit (§ 20.3)."}
